stimulus:
Information and consent

This study is part of a university course project on how people use advice from artificial intelligence (AI). You will look at 28 small pictures of everyday objects, say what each one shows, and see the answer of an AI image-recognition system, in 5 short rounds. You will also answer a few quick questions. It takes about 8–10 minutes.

Participation is voluntary and unpaid. You may stop at any time without giving a reason. Your answers are stored under a participant number only; no name or contact details are recorded. The anonymised data will be used for the course project and may be shared in anonymised form.

Do you agree to take part?

Round 1 of 5

Thank you — debriefing

This study compares different ways of showing how confident an AI is. Half of the participants worked with an AI whose confidence values were honest (calibrated): when it said 80%, it was right about 80% of the time. The other half worked with the same AI, giving the same answers, but its confidence values were deliberately inflated (overconfident), so it often said it was very sure even when it was wrong. You were in the overconfident group.

We did not tell you this in advance because we wanted to see how people react to overconfident AI. The AI's answers themselves were real outputs of an image-recognition model. Please do not tell other students about the two groups until the study is finished.
